channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Carnell Tate (shoulder) returned to practice on Wednesday.
item.description: Tate missed Week 8 because of the shoulder issue. He got the bye week to recover but still wasn’t able to suit up in Week 10. Robert Saleh told reporters on Tuesday that he is hoping Tate is ready to go for Sunday’s game. Even a limited practice today would put him on track to play. With Wan’Dale Robinson on IR, Tate will return to an elite target share, even if he’s not fully healthy. He will be in the WR3 mix if the team clears him for Week 11.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Darren Waller (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description: Waller is sometimes given Wednesdays often, so this could just be precautionary. Panthers backup TE Tommy Tremble (knee) was also listed as a non-participant. Hopefully, one of them is good to go for this week’s game against the Ravens.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Mike Jackson (groin) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Ravens.
item.description: Panthers coach Dave Canales told reporters that he thinks Jackson, his team’s No. 2 perimeter cornerback, is “ready” to return. He will slightly upgrade the Panthers’ secondary if so. Jackson has been sidelined since injuring his groin in late September.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Ravens.
item.description: The Panthers listed Brooks as a full participant for two practices last week before amending his participation to limited at the end of the week. We doubt they’ll do that again. Panthers coach Dave Canales told reporters today that he thinks Brooks is “ready.” He can be speculatively stashed in 12-team leagues.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Bryce Young (foot) is practicing in full for Week 11 against the Ravens.
item.description: Young has played through lower-body injuries for much of the season already. Late in October, coach Dave Canales admitted that Young’s knee issue may be limiting his mobility. While we fully expect Young to play this week, he may be a little less likely to scramble than he normally would. Regardless, it doesn’t alter his ranking much. Today, Canales said Young’s “foot was sore coming out of the game Sunday, but it’s been getting better and better.”-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Texans ruled out Danielle Hunter (hamstring) for Week 11 against the Colts.
item.description: Hunter will now miss his second game due to a hamstring injury. He is replaced in the lineup by veteran pass rusher Jadaveon Clowney. Fortunately, Will Anderson returned from his ankle injury last week. Kamari Lassiter (wrist) is expected to play.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Texans ruled out Marvin Harrison (hamstring) for Week 11 against the Colts.
item.description: Unfortunately, the Texans’ mid-season acquisition will miss another game. Harrison’s absence helpfully condenses the pass-catching corps for fantasy football purposes, though. Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson will likely lead their position group, followed by Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Texans ruled out Woody Marks (concussion) for Week 11 against the Colts.
item.description: David Montgomery (groin) is expected to return for tomorrow’s game. Emari Demercardo will serve as Montgomery’s backup. The Texans’ run game has been unable to establish itself as a reliable unit, but Montgomery’s workload and matchup against the Colts’ defense put him in the RB2 tier. The Texans face the Ravens in Week 12. Should Marks return to action, he will likely be relegated to PPR FLEX status.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Steelers placed LG Mason McCormick (ankle) on injured reserve.
item.description: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports this morning that McCormick suffered a dislocated ankle but not a fracture. That gives him a shot at returning in the postseason, though he will miss at least the rest of the regular season. Spencer Anderson took his spot in the lineup on Sunday and will likely do so going forward.-Kyle Dvorchak
